messages.content:
You are grading an AI assistant's answer to a question about a company handbook.

Question: How many days of paid leave does a new father receive in GitLab Korea Limited for bonding with his child?
Reference answer (written from the handbook): 10 days

Passages the assistant was given:
"""
[GitLab Korea Limited Benefits > We've Got You Covered > Growing Family Leaves > Paternity Leave]
10 days of paid leave for new fathers to bond with their child and support their partner. If you are eligible, you will receive 100% paid Parental Leave from GitLab up to 16 weeks.

Leave Entitlement

- **Statutory Entitlment**: 10 calendar days to Use within 90 days of birth
- **Flexible Usage**: Take consecutively or split into two periods
- **100% Paid**: Full salary continuation through GitLab

[GitLab BV (Netherlands) Benefits > We've Got You Covered > Growing Families Leaves > Statutory Partner/Paternity Leave]
Time to bond with your new child and support your partner.

Leave Entitlement

* 5 days paid Birth Leave (100% salary), to be used within 4 weeks of birth
* 5 weeks paid Additional Birth Leave within 6 months (at 70% of maximum day wage)
* Review [company policy](/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave) as when more beneficial they supersede the statutory leave benefits

How to Access

1. Email [leaves@gitlab.com](mailto:leaves@gitlab.com) with your desired dates
1. Request the additional 5 weeks at least 4 weeks in advance

[GitLab Ireland Ltd > We've Got You Covered > Growing Family Leaves > Paternity Leave]
Time to bond with your newborn.  

Eligibility

- Father of the child  
- Partner of the mother  
- Parent of donor-conceived child

  

Leave Entitlement

- 2 consecutive weeks within first 6 months  
- State Paternity Benefit: €262/week (subject to PRSI)  
- GitLab tops up to 100% salary

  

How to Apply

1. Notify leaves@gitlab.com with due date
2. Receive PB2 form from Absence Management
3. Apply via [gov.ie](https://www.gov.ie/en/service/apply-for-paternity-benefit/) at least 4 weeks before leave

[GitLab LTD (UK) Benefits > We've Got You Covered > Growing Family leaves > Adoption Leave]
Leave Entitlement

- Up to 52 weeks leave available
- Team members can receive statutory adoption pay for up to 39 weeks
- Team members must have had continuous employment with GitLab for at least 26 weeks leading up to the week they were matched with the child.
- Eligible team members are entitled to 90% of your average weekly earnings (before tax) for the first 6 weeks, £194.32 or 90% of your average weekly earnings (whichever is lower) for the next 33 weeks

How to Apply

- Submit leave request in Workday (Parental Leave Category) 30+ days before start
- Provide proof of the adoption or surrogacy to leaves@gitlab.com
- The Absence Management team will notify payroll and email Vistra a copy of the form, dates of leave and outline what pay the team member is eligible for (statutory, supplemental, etc)

[GitLab Korea Limited Benefits > We've Got You Covered > Growing Family Leaves > Extended Parental Leave (Child Care Leave)]
Up to one year of additional leave for ongoing childcare needs, available to eligible parents. Extended leave of up to 18 months may be available in certain circumstances.

Eligibility Requirements

- Minimum of six months of GitLab employment prior to scheduled leave start date
- Child must be eight years old or younger, or in second grade or below in elementary school
- Pregnant employees may apply to protect their pregnancy
- Parents cannot take leave simultaneously

Leave Entitlement

- **Duration**: Up to one year per parent
- **Extended Duration**: Up to 18 months total for parents who qualify under any of the following:

- Both parents have taken at least three months of childcare leave each for the same child
- Single parents as defined under the Single-Parent Family Support Act
- Parents of a child with a qualifying disability as prescribed by the Ministry of Employment and Labor

- **Insurance Support**: 40% salary from Employment Insurance Fund
- **GitLab Supplement**: Additional support to reach 100% pay for up to 16 weeks (if eligible under [GitLab's Parental Leave policy](/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/leave-types/#gitlab-parental-leave))

[GitLab Korea Limited Benefits > We've Got You Covered > Growing Family Leaves > Family Care Leave]
Leave to care for family members due to illness, accident, old age, or to care for a child.

Eligibility Requirements

- Minimum six months of GitLab employment
- Available for care of parent, grandparent, grandchild, child, spouse, or parent-in-law

Leave Entitlement

- **Short-term Family Care Leave**: Up to 10 days per year (unpaid), can be split over multiple occasions
- **Extended Family Care Leave**: Up to 90 days per year (unpaid), including any short-term leave taken. Minimum 30 days must be used at a time for extended leave.
- **How to Request**: Please provide advanced notice when possible. You can submit a Compass case to the Absence Management team for more information.

Important Dates/Details

- **Advance Notice**: 30 days required for all parental leave types
- **Documentation**: Medical certificates required for maternity leave
- **Coordination**: Work with Total Rewards team for insurance claims
"""

Assistant's answer:
"""
A new father at GitLab Korea Limited receives 10 days of paid leave to bond with their child and support their partner [1].
"""

First write one sentence of reasoning, then grade three things:
- correctness: "correct" if the answer states the key information in the reference answer without contradicting it (extra correct detail is fine); "partial" if it gets part of it or is vague; "incorrect" if it is wrong, contradicts the reference, or does not answer.
- refused: true if the assistant declined or said it does not know, instead of answering.
- faithful: true if every factual claim in the answer is supported by the passages above (ignore whether it matches the reference). An answer that only refuses counts as faithful.
The grades must agree with your reasoning.
Return JSON with the reasoning first: {"reason": "one sentence", "correctness": "correct" | "partial" | "incorrect", "refused": true/false, "faithful": true/false}
